decisions.reason: Define-XML ADQSNPIX.EFFFL names ADSL.FASFL, while the submitted ADSL has EFFFL and no FASFL; the specification reads ADSL_LKP.EFFFL.
SAP page-11 explicitly calls the telephone visit output labels Week 10/14/18/22 (Tel), while Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVISIT enumerates the corresponding labels without (Tel).

Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVISIT supplies the same visit identities and mappings as the reference after leading padding is removed; every literal difference pattern is padding alone. The probe adds an unpadded layout requirement that the documented character-label rule does not state.
Define-XML ADQSNPIX.PARAM and ADQSNPIX.PARAMCD spell the Hallucination label with one internal blank before Score; PARAM__LITERAL faithfully uses it and the evidence shows two in the reference.

Define-XML ADQSNPIX.PARAM enumerates the Hallucination coded value with one internal blank before Score, while both data sides contain two; trimming the value does not remove that internal difference.

SAP page-10 states LOCF for missing postbaseline efficacy values without an NPI-X exception, while the NPI-X paragraph of dataguide page-7 explicitly says LOCF was not used. SAP page-15 describes available-score averaging but does not expressly withdraw the general imputation instruction.
SAP page-10 requires LOCF for missing postbaseline efficacy values, whereas dataguide page-7 explicitly excludes LOCF for NPI-X; the retained statements differ in applicability as written.

Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AWTDIFF states the absolute difference without a composite-row exception. AWTDIFF__LITERAL faithfully leaves that arithmetic missing when ADY is missing, whereas the evidence shows zero for the aggregate rows.
Define-XML ADQSNPIX.STUDYID and dataguide page-4 explicitly name ADSL as the source; natural reads QS.STUDYID, so the stated source differs even when the identifiers agree.
Define-XML ADQSNPIX.USUBJID and dataguide page-4 name ADSL.USUBJID; natural instead reads QS.USUBJID.
Define-XML ADQSNPIX.USUBJID names ADSL.USUBJID, while nptotmn_base takes MIN(QS.USUBJID) within the QS subject group.
Dataguide page-4 says USUBJID was merged from ADSL into all analysis datasets; nptotmn_mean instead obtains it by MIN(QS.USUBJID).

In natural, ADY is assigned QS.QSDY and _WINDOW is computed from that identical value, so Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVISITN does have an ADY-based counterpart. Whether that assigned ADY satisfies its own documented date formula is the separate ADY finding.

SAP page-11 specifies visit date minus randomization date; natural uses QS.QSDY without a randomization-date subtraction. Native SDTM COMPMETHOD.STUDY_DAY instead anchors QSDY to RFSTDTC and adds one on or after that date, so it does not supply the missing SAP computation.

Define-XML ADQSNPIX.ADY explicitly anchors the formula to TRTSDT, but natural copies QS.QSDY. Native SDTM COMPMETHOD.STUDY_DAY uses RFSTDTC, and the retained ADSL.TRTSDT rule names the visit-3 SV date, so the governing sources do not establish the same anchor by definition.
Define-XML ADQSNPIX.PARAMCD maps NPITM02S to a label with one internal blank before Score; natural explicitly emits two blanks for that code.

SAP page-15 defines the mean over Weeks 4 through 24 inclusive, but W3_LKP through W6_LKP select _WINDOW 3 through 6, which natural maps to Weeks 6, 8, 10, and 12. nptotmn_mean averages only those lookups.

Dataguide page-7 gives NPTOTMN to patients with assessments anywhere in Weeks 4 through 24; nptotmn_mean requires a nonmissing result in W3_LKP through W6_LKP only. Those lookups cover only Weeks 6 through 12, so the availability condition is narrower.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVAL.NPTOT directs AVAL to QS.QSSTRESN, and native SDTM COMPMETHOD.QSAD_QSSTRESN explicitly delegates NPI-X total scoring to the SAP. The natural QS numeric copy therefore consumes the SAP-derived total; this ADaM specification need not reconstruct the frequency-by-severity score and excluded domains.

Native SDTM QS.QSTESTCD.NPTOT and COMPMETHOD.QSAD_QSSTRESN state that the source total is derived according to the SAP, including page-47 domain scoring. Native ADaM ADQSNPIX.AVAL.NPTOT then specifies a QS.QSSTRESN copy, which natural implements.

Native SDTM COMPMETHOD.QSAD_QSSTRESN delegates the NPI-X total to the SAP, which includes the page-47 missing-item threshold and scale adjustment. Native ADQSNPIX.AVAL.NPTOT and natural both use that computed QS numeric total, so this is upstream scoring rather than an absent ADaM computation.
Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AWTDIFF specifies ABS(AWTARGET-ADY) without a parameter exception; nptotmn_mean clears ADY but explicitly assigns _AWTDIFF=0.0.
Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVISIT and SAP page-11 state visit labels, but neither specifies the leading-blank alignment implemented in natural; the original ItemDef length does not prescribe that alignment.

SAP page-11 does not bind its randomization-date anchor to an input field, and Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVISITN instead references treatment-relative ADY. The codelist and dataguide page-7 identify composite baseline and mean visits but do not fully state the record conditions that extend the assessment-day rule to those rows.

Define-XML ADQSNPIX.ADT requires a SAS date from QS.QSDTC, while natural additionally fills an incomplete month and day with 1. Neither the NPI-X source sections nor native QS.QSDTC states that imputation convention.

Define-XML ADQSNPIX.ADT states the QS.QSDTC conversion, and dataguide page-7 identifies NPTOTMN as a derived mean, but neither explicitly assigns missing ADT and ADY to its aggregate row as nptotmn_mean does.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVAL.NPITM01S through ADQSNPIX.AVAL.NPTOT explicitly match QSTESTCD to the given PARAMCD, and dataguide page-7 identifies QS as their source. That equality, together with the ADQSNPIX.PARAMCD codelist, documents the ordinary code correspondence implemented by PARAMCD: QS.QSTESTCD.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.PARAMTYP.NPITM01S through .NPTOT instruct missing, and .NPTOTMN instructs DERIVED. The whole branch rule is retained; its omission from the exported ADQSNPIX.PARAMTYP section is a source-interface limitation, not an incomplete derivation.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AVAL.NPITM01S through .NPTOT names QS.QSSTRESN and .NPTOTMN specifies the Week 4-24 mean; dataguide page-7 supplies the baseline exception. These retained instructions support the ordinary and composite arithmetic, so the stated citation-interface omission does not establish an incomplete documented rule.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.BASE.NPITM01S through .NPTOT names QS.QSSTRESN when QSBLFL=Y, and .NPTOTMN additionally specifies QSTESTCD=NPTOT. Those are the source and baseline conditions omitted from the exported section; their absence from that interface is not absent documentation.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.CHG.NPITM01S through .NPTOT states AVAL-BASE for postbaseline records, and .NPTOTMN requires missing. The exported section omits a retained whole-variable rule; the specification failing to apply its baseline/composite gating is a separate issue.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.PCHG.NPITM01S through .NPTOT states 100*(CHG/BASE) for postbaseline records, and .NPTOTMN requires missing. The arithmetic and applicability are retained, with undefined zero-baseline division remaining missing; this finding reflects an omitted source interface.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.ABLFL.NPITM01S through .NPTOT specifies QS.QSBLFL, and .NPTOTMN explicitly requires missing without a baseline exception. This is a complete retained branch rule omitted by the exported section, even though nptotmn_base assigns Y contrary to it.

SAP page-11 resolves equal distance by the pre-target day, and dataguide page-7 states closest-target selection; neither gives a sequence-number tie rule for assessments on the same day. Native ANL01FL value-level instructions add no QSSEQ rule.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.ANL01FL.NPTOTMN explicitly assigns Y, while the ordinary ItemDefs refer to the SAP windows and dataguide page-7 explains the analysis flag. The composite instruction identified as missing in this finding is retained and omitted only from the exported section; the additional same-day tie policy is reviewed separately.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.DTYPE.NPITM01S through .NPTOT instructs missing and .NPTOTMN specifies AVERAGE. The original XML supplies the complete parameter-specific assignments that the exported codelist-only section omits.

Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AWTARGET and SAP page-11 provide scheduled assessment target days, while ADQSNPIX.AVISITN gives 98 as a visit code. None states that 98 is a relative target day for the derived mean, as nptotmn_mean assigns.

SAP page-11 fully supplies scheduled visit targets, but neither it nor dataguide page-7 gives a target day for the Weeks 4-24 aggregate. Native ADQSNPIX.AWTARGET contains no additional composite instruction, so the whole-column rule leaves that case unstated.

SAP page-11 leaves the baseline beginning unbounded and Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AWLO only refers to the SAP start day; neither prescribes its numeric encoding. The Week 4-24 period permits a union-window reading, but does not supply the missing open-end representation convention.

SAP page-11 leaves the Week 26 ending unbounded and Define-XML ADQSNPIX.AWHI only refers to the SAP end day; neither prescribes its numeric encoding. The native ItemDef adds no endpoint instruction, so an exact whole-column representation remains unstated.

Native Define-XML ADQSNPIX.QSSEQ.NPITM01S through .NPTOT specifies QS.QSSEQ, and .NPTOTMN distinguishes missing postbaseline sequences from the QS BASELINE/NPTOT source sequence. Native SDTM QS.QSBLFL also explicitly identifies VISIT=BASELINE, so the retained source condition is documented despite its omission from the exported section.
